How do tracing, evaluations, and Signals fit together?

smart_toy

Tracing records what your application or agent does. Evaluations measure quality on a fixed set of test examples. Signals score the agent activity you've traced in production. Put together: tracing is the record of what happened, and evaluations and Signals are two ways of judging it.

Tracing: capturing activity

For agents, the Weave SDK records the whole multi-turn conversation: each user–agent exchange (a "turn"), the LLM calls inside it, and the tools those calls run. Each step is saved as a span, which is a record of one operation, and appears in the Agents tab [S6].
The point is to let you "view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior" [S6]. Conversation views show turns, LLM calls, tool runs, token counts and any attached feedback [S7].
(If you trace plain functions with @weave.op instead, Weave groups the recorded calls into Traces, which are trees of calls [S2][S5].)

Evaluations: measuring on fixed test cases

An Evaluation combines a dataset of test examples with one or more scoring functions. You run it against a model or function, and each .evaluate() creates an evaluation run [S3].
You use evaluations to compare changes over time and catch regressions (cases where quality got worse) [S3].

Signals: scoring live traffic

Signals score agent turns and apply tags or ratings (a rating is a 0.0–1.0 score attached to a matching span) to surface quality and safety issues in production [S1][S4].
Examples include scoring answer quality, noticing user frustration, or flagging NSFW content. Results appear in the Signals tab of the Agents view and highlight the traces that need attention [S1].

How they connect

Evaluations and tracing: while an evaluation runs, Weave automatically captures a trace of each prediction and each score, so you can inspect every one in the UI [S8].
Signals and tracing: Signals work on traced agent activity. They tag and rate spans and highlight the traces worth reviewing [S1][S4].
Evaluations vs. Signals: evaluations test against examples you choose, to compare versions [S3]. Signals keep an eye on your agent's conversations in production [S1].
